The workspace keeps every draft, review and decision in one place, so a team that picks up a project after a month away can read how it got to where it is without asking anyone who was there at the time.

Each record carries its own history. A change shows who made it and what it replaced, and a reviewer can step back through the versions one at a time until the point where the numbers stopped adding up.

Access follows the work. A contractor sees the two projects they were brought in for and nothing else, and when the engagement ends their access ends with it, on the date written into the invitation.

Exports are plain files in open formats. Nothing is held in a shape only this product can read, and a team that decides to leave takes its whole archive along in an afternoon without writing to support.

Alerts go to the person on call and to nobody else. The schedule is a table anyone on the team can read, and swapping a shift takes two taps from the phone, with the change noted for the rest of the week.

Billing counts active seats on the last day of the month. A seat that was added and removed inside the same month costs nothing, and the invoice lists each seat by name so finance can check it line by line.
